current.text: He has a broken foot and will not be ready for the start of the season. Yahoo lists him as questionable (foot).
Josh expects him back around Thanksgiving, followed by a slow ramp-up.
Daniel Gafford is the likely opening night center. Gafford and Morez Johnson Jr. are ahead of Lively in the rotation, and Josh's projected starting five has Johnson at center.
Dusty May is the new head coach. It is unknown how he will split center minutes between Lively, Gafford, Powell, Johnson and forwards like Washington and Aldama.
Josh finds him almost impossible to draft in 10, 12 or 14 team leagues and says to ignore his ADP of 107. His health and playing time are uncertain.
He becomes a draftable fantasy player only if he wins a starting job.
He is in the last year of his contract and becomes a restricted free agent next offseason.
Dallas has a 4-4-4 schedule in our fantasy playoff weeks, probably the best in the league. It also has the league-high 16 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He has a long history of lower-body injuries. His games played have fallen every season since his rookie year, and injuries have derailed his career.
When healthy, he blocks shots at a high level, rebounds well and is a strong defender. He is a good roller and is very good in the short roll.
His category profile is a very high FG% and strong blocks, with no threes. His FT% is poor, but he takes few free throws.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both value him at 0 USD (ranks 166 and 143), and Josh says to ignore his ADP of 107. Do not spend on him at our auction, even though he cost 3 USD last season. He is a waiver watch: he has a broken foot and is out until around Thanksgiving, then ramps up slowly behind Gafford and Johnson. If he wins the starting job later, his strong FG% and blocks with no threes fit a punt 3PM build, and Dallas has a 4-4-4 playoff schedule.
